Different machinery. Connected outputs.

How they meet

People review an LLM’s prompts. An image can guide a video’s first frame. Music and dialogue join the edited clip. ComfyUI connects compatible node outputs to inputs; it does not turn every model into one algorithm.

03 / THE CREATIVE COST

Would you release it?

Try five production decisions. The strongest workflow includes consent, review and responsibility.

Our group’s pros & cons

World building

For fantasy and sci-fi movies, AI could quickly generate backdrops and action instead of requiring some real sets and props. [1]

Consistent style & props

It is hard to keep props and style consistent throughout a movie. With AI videos, referencing images can help, though results still need checking. [1,3]

Low cost for redos

AI-generated shots can be cheaper and easier to regenerate than traditional reshoots, which may require rebuilding sets and recalling crews. [1]

Teaching & demonstrations

Supports teaching and topic demonstrations (e.g., Google NotebookLM), which could produce teaching videos and slide decks. [26]

Creative ideas

Lets people imagine themselves or their IPs in different situations, making prompts a strong source of creative ideas. [1]

Low variety

The base model could produce very similar scenes or characters. Copying others’ work or using someone’s likeness without permission can raise rights concerns. [5,20]

Deepfake abuse

Shorts could feature real people in undesirable or sexual settings, harming their reputations. Videos of loved ones may be used to threaten or scam family members. [19,23]

Labour & consent

AI could affect traditional film workers’ jobs, wages and creative control. Reusing someone’s appearance or voice raises consent and credit concerns. [6,20]

Reality or fiction?

As AI videos become more realistic, people may become confused about what is real and more vulnerable to fake news. [21]

Revenue limits

YouTube may reject repetitively produced AI junk, while people making similar videos may also face monetisation restrictions. [10]

Numbers refer to the full bibliography. These are the captions from our poster.

Our recommendation

The best outcome: Use AI tools for filmmaking, but add invisible watermarks for identification and notifications if a video is inappropriate. This could help platforms quickly remove AI junk and help people distinguish real news from fake news.

The 2023 Hollywood labour disputes brought digital replicas and control of creative work into the industry debate. Industry source [15] ↗
